study_identification_part.si3_author_journal_year: Joo SW, Jo YT, Kim Y, Lee WH, Chung Y-C, Lee J (2023). Structural variability of the cerebral cortex in schizophrenia and its association with clinical symptoms. Psychological Medicine 1 -10.
study_identification_part.si4_title: Structural variability of the cerebral cortex in schizophrenia and its association with clinical symptoms

study_characteristics_part.sc1_study_objective: To investigate the structural variability of the cerebral cortex in patients with schizophrenia compared to healthy controls using data from seven studies, and to examine its association with clinical symptoms and cognitive functions.

rci1_dataset_name.reason: The paper explicitly lists these seven datasets in the 'Study population' section.
rci1_dataset_name.supporting_text: We included neuroimaging datasets acquired from two tertiary hospitals in the Republic of Korea, the Asan Medical Center (AMC) and Jeonbuk National University Hospital (JNUH). Several publicly available neuroimaging datasets were used in this study. From the SchizConnect database (http://schizconnect. org) (Wang et al., 2016), we obtained Center of Biomedical Research Excellence (COBRE), Neuromorphometry by Computer Algorithm Chicago (NMorphCH), MIND Clinical Imaging Consortium (MCIC), and Function Biomedical Informatics Research Network (fBIRN) datasets. Neuroimaging and clinical data from University of California Los Angeles Consortium for Neuropsychiatric Phenomics LA5c Study (UCLA) were downloaded from OpenNeuro (http://openneuro. org) with the accession number ds000030.

nm5_predictor_variables.reason: The study uses a Person-Based Similarity Index (PBSI) which calculates the correlation of an individual's morphometric profile with the average profile of the reference group. This method does not use predictor variables like age or sex to model the response variable; instead, it generates a similarity score for each individual, and the distribution of these scores in the control group serves as the normative model. The paper later regresses out the effects of age when correlating PBSI with illness duration, but age is not a predictor in the normative model itself.
nm5_predictor_variables.supporting_text: In each group, the cortical structural profile of an individual correlated with the respective profiles of all other individuals within the same group using the Spearman ' s correlation coefficient rho. This process yielded n -1 correlation coefficients per participant, where n is the number of participants in the same group. The correlation coefficients were then averaged to generate the PBSI score...
nm5_predictor_variables.location: Joo2024.pdf.md: Global variability of cortical measures

nm6_predictor_effects.reason: As explained for nm5_predictor_variables, the PBSI method used in this study does not involve predictor variables, so there are no predictor effects to describe.

clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa7_association_analysis: Group differences in continuous variables were tested using Student's t-test or Mann-Whitney U test. Chi-square tests were used for categorical variables. Group differences in the CV were tested using an asymptotic test. Spearman's correlation was used to test the association between the PBSI score and clinical variables. The effects of age were regressed out for the association between illness duration and PBSI score. Patients were divided into 'deviant' and 'other' based on a z-score of the PBSI score, and PANSS scores and neurocognitive results were compared using the Mann-Whitney U test. Bonferroni correction was used for multiple testing.
clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa8_key_findings_brief: Patients with schizophrenia showed greater regional and global structural variability of the cerebral cortex than healthy controls, and this deviation in structural similarity was associated with lower general intelligence.
clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa9_key_findings_detailed: Patients with schizophrenia (SCZ) had a higher coefficient of variation (CV) of surface area and cortical thickness in some cortical regions compared to healthy controls (HC). All Person-Based Similarity Index (PBSI) scores across four cortical measures (surface area, gray matter volume, thickness, local gyrification index) were lower in patients with SCZ than in HCs, indicating greater heterogeneity. In the patient group, PBSI scores for gray matter volume (PBSI-GV) and all measures combined (PBSI-All) were positively correlated with full-scale IQ scores. Patients with 'deviant' PBSI-GV and PBSI-All scores (z < -1.5 relative to HC) had significantly lower IQ scores than other patients.

caa10_key_limitations.answer: 1. The significant association between PBSI and IQ scores was based on a small subset of patients. 2. The harmonization process did not consider variations from race, cognitive function, and education. 3. Cumulative exposure to antipsychotic medications was not considered. 4. A comprehensive analysis of cognitive functions was not possible due to a limited number of cognitive tests.
caa10_key_limitations.supporting_text: Several limitations should be considered when interpreting these results. First, the significant associations between the PBSI-GV, PBSI-All, and IQ scores in patients with schizophrenia was derived based on a small subset of patients for whom the IQ scores were available... Second, we did not consider morphometric measure variations derived from different sample characteristics in terms of race, cognitive function, and education in the harmonization process... Third, cumulative exposure to antipsychotic medications was not considered... Fourth, we could not perform a comprehensive analysis of the associations of the PBSI scores with cognitive functions because of the limited number of cognitive tests.

clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa11_application_notes: The study used the Person-Based Similarity Index (PBSI) to quantify global structural variability at an individual level. A finer-grained cortical parcellation (308 regions) was used compared to standard atlases. The local gyrification index was included as a morphometric measure in addition to more common measures.

general_note_part.gn1_general_notes: This study is a large-scale analysis that pools neuroimaging data from seven different studies (two local, five public) to investigate brain structural variability in schizophrenia. Site effects across the datasets were harmonized using ComBat.
